correctness.rationale: Represent vertices of Z4xZ4 by 0..15; define the r=2 faces exactly by induced maximum degree <=1, forbidding any selected center with two selected neighbors (triangles also prohibited). Exhaustively enumerate all 65536 masks per graph, yielding Shrikhande face numbers [1,16,120,384,544,240,32], rook [1,16,120,384,528,144]. For common pivot order (9,2,13,7,12,6,15,14,8,3,0,10,4,1,11,5), independent full Hasse-graph construction finds 639 and 543 matched pairs, 4960 and 4224 directed incidences, and verifies acyclicity by complete topological sort. Critical cells are a single 0-cell and 57 vs 105 3-cells. Forman discrete Morse theory produces a CW complex with those cell counts; every 3-cell attaches to the one-point 2-skeleton, hence a wedge of S3 integrally. This is a complete finite proof certificate over all faces, not inference from partial enumeration or modular Betti numbers.

value.rationale: These two cospectral nonisomorphic strongly regular graphs are a canonical test pair. The reverse strict inequality between ordinary and two-independence sphere multiplicities is a motivated homotopy-level distinction not given by SRG parameters or the ordinary independence calculation. A finite exact homotopy computation is itself a useful invariant.

final_claim: For the two strongly regular (16,6,2,2) graphs, the two-independence/dissociation complex is integrally homotopy equivalent to 57 copies of S3 for Shrikhande and 105 copies of S3 for the 4x4 rook graph. Ordinary r=1 sphere counts 23 and 15 are previously known and reverse this order.
